change.title: ao-replay/9095-r2
change.description: fix(agents): list nested Claude commands and dedupe plugins by resolved name
change.author: ronish

findings.title: Symlinked commands folder now yields no commands
findings.body: The old code listed a commands root with `os.ReadDir(root.dir)`, which follows a symlink at the root. The new `commandFiles` uses `filepath.WalkDir`, which calls `os.Lstat` on the root and does not follow a symlink there. If `~/.claude/commands` or `<workspace>/.claude/commands` is a symlink to a directory (common with dotfile managers), the callback sees one non-directory entry named `commands`. That entry does not end in `.md`, so the function returns nothing. The user's commands silently vanish from the pre-session `/` menu. The skills branch still uses `os.ReadDir` plus `os.Stat`, so only commands regress. Resolve the root first, for example with `filepath.EvalSymlinks(dir)`, before walking, or walk the path with a trailing separator. Add a test with a symlinked commands root.

findings.title: Nested-command coverage skips plugin prefixes, dotted subfolders and symlinks
findings.body: The new tests cover a nested command only in a project root. They do not cover a plugin commands root, where the name must come out as `plugin:ns:cmd`. They do not cover hidden subfolders being skipped by `commandFiles`. They do not cover a symlinked commands directory, which behaves differently under `WalkDir` than it did under `ReadDir`.

contracts.action: Commands roots are enumerated recursively with filepath.WalkDir; nested commands are named path:with:colons
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous os.ReadDir-based flat listing in scanSkillRoots (same file, removed lines)
contracts.before_after: Before: ReadDir followed a symlinked root and listed only top-level .md files. After: WalkDir recurses into subfolders but does not follow a symlinked root, and it skips hidden subfolders.
contracts.visible_effect: The chat `/` menu shows nested commands such as `ns:deep-cmd` before the agent starts, but would show none for a symlinked commands root.
contracts.failure_mode: Errors inside the walk are swallowed by returning nil, so an unreadable folder gives a silent partial list. A symlinked root gives an empty list, which the user cannot see as a failure.

contracts.action: Plugin dedup moved from install key to resolved manifest name
contracts.equivalent_path: Same enabledClaudePlugins loop before the change, which deduped on the key name and on the resolved name only with a `break` that skipped the append
contracts.before_after: Before: a plugin whose manifest name matched an earlier one dropped the whole entry, and the key-name check could hide a plugin that resolved to a different name. After: only the resolved name is checked, and the loop still breaks after the first applicable install.
contracts.visible_effect: Plugins whose manifest names differ from their keys each contribute their prefixed skills.

summary: I found one regression, in the new `commandFiles`. `filepath.WalkDir` does not follow a symlink at the root, so a commands folder that is itself a symlink now lists nothing where the old `os.ReadDir` code listed its commands. The plugin dedup change looks correct and its test covers it. The new tests don't cover plugin-prefixed nested commands, hidden subfolders or symlinks.
